sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「此不過屬吏為一郡一邑之說，汝等封疆大吏，不可存遏糶之心。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "This is merely what subordinates say for one commandery or one county; you territorial grand officers must not harbor a mind to block the sale of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is merely what subordinates say on behalf of one commandery or one county; you territorial grand officers must not harbor any wish to block grain sales.

sentences.zh: 若無米可販，百姓自不運，何待汝等禁乎？」

translations.literal: If there is no rice to sell, the people will not transport it of themselves—why wait for you to forbid it?"
translations.idiomatic: If there is no rice to sell, the people will not transport it on their own—why should you need to forbid it?"

sentences.zh: 又言兗、沂等府州被水，而江南饑民復至，疏請無災州縣留養限五百人，有災州縣限二三百人，上命實力料理。

translations.literal: He also reported that Yanzhou, Yizhou, and other prefectures suffered flooding while famine refugees from Jiangnan arrived again; he memorialized asking that disaster-free prefectures and counties limit relief to five hundred persons and disaster-stricken ones to two or three hundred; the emperor ordered diligent handling.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported flooding in Yanzhou, Yizhou, and other prefectures while famine refugees from Jiangnan arrived again; he memorialized asking disaster-free prefectures and counties to limit relief to five hundred persons and disaster-stricken ones to two or three hundred; the emperor ordered them handled diligently.

sentences.zh: 八年，調湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1743) he was transferred to governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷戶部侍郎，仍留任。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to vice minister of Revenue while retaining his governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to vice minister of Revenue while retaining his governorship.

sentences.zh: 斯盛究心民事，屢陳救濟民食諸疏​​，以社倉保甲相為經緯，因言：「周禮族師、遂人之法，稽其實則井田為之經。

translations.literal: Sisheng devoted himself to the people's affairs and repeatedly submitted memorials on relieving the people's food supply, taking community granaries and baojia as mutually warp and weft; he therefore said: "The Rites of Zhou methods of clan masters and district officers—in examining their substance, the well-field system was their warp.
translations.idiomatic: Sisheng devoted himself to the people's welfare and repeatedly submitted memorials on relieving food shortages, treating community granaries and baojia as mutually reinforcing institutions; he argued: "The Rites of Zhou methods of clan masters and district officers, when examined in substance, took the well-field system as their foundation.

sentences.zh: 蓋就相生相養之地，而行政教法令於其中。

translations.literal: It was taking land where mutual production and mutual nurture occurred, and administering government, teaching, and ordinances within it.
translations.idiomatic: Government, teaching, and law were administered within lands where people mutually produced and supported one another.

sentences.zh: 是以習其事而不覺，久於其道而不變。

translations.literal: Thus people practiced the affairs without awareness, and long accustomed to the Way without change.
translations.idiomatic: People practiced these affairs without noticing it and grew long accustomed to the way without change.

sentences.zh: 週衰，管子作軌裡連鄉，小治而未大效。

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, Guanzi made the linked-township grain-control system; there was minor order but no great effect.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined, Guan Zhong established the linked-township grain-control system, which brought minor order but no great effect.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢、隋、唐，龐雜無紀。

translations.literal: Qin, Han, Sui, and Tang were sprawling and complex without coherent order.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin, Han, Sui, and Tang the systems grew sprawling and lacked coherent order.

sentences.zh: 宋熙寧中，編閭里之戶為保甲，事本近古，然亦第相保相受，而未得其相生相養之經。

translations.literal: In the Xining era of Song, households of villages and neighborhoods were organized as baojia; the matter was essentially close to antiquity, yet it was only mutual guarantee and mutual liability, without attaining the warp of mutual production and mutual nurture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xining era of Song, village and neighborhood households were organized as baojia, which in principle looked back to antiquity, yet amounted only to mutual guarantee and mutual liability without attaining the foundation of mutual production and mutual support.

sentences.zh: 臣前奏推廣社倉之法，請按堡設倉，使人有所恃，安土重遷，保甲聯比，相為經緯。

translations.literal: Your subject previously memorialized to extend the community granary method, asking to establish granaries by fort, so people have something to rely on, cling to their land and value relocation, and baojia are linked as warp and weft.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject previously memorialized to extend the community granary system by establishing granaries in each fort, so that people would have something to rely on, cling to their land and hesitate to move away, and baojia units would be linked as mutually reinforcing institutions.

sentences.zh: 顧欲各堡一倉，倉積穀三千，一時既有難行；

translations.literal: But wishing one granary per fort, each storing three thousand shi of grain, is hard to carry out at once;
translations.idiomatic: Yet establishing one granary in every fort, each storing three thousand shi of grain, would be hard to carry out all at once;

sentences.zh: 而入穀之數，則變通於額賦之中，別分本折，稍覺紛更。

translations.literal: and the amount of grain contributed would be adjusted within the quota tax, separately dividing original and cash conversion—a slight sense of confusion and change.
translations.idiomatic: and adjusting the amount of grain contributed within the quota tax by separately dividing grain and cash payments would feel somewhat disruptive.

sentences.zh: 雖然，社倉保甲，原有相通之理，亦有兼及之勢。

translations.literal: Even so, community granaries and baojia originally have a principle of interconnection, and also a tendency toward mutual inclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, community granaries and baojia originally share a principle of interconnection and a tendency toward mutual reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 求備誠難，試行或易。

translations.literal: Seeking perfection is truly hard; trial implementation may be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking a perfect system is truly difficult; a trial implementation may be easier.

sentences.zh: 加意倉儲，既慮貴糶妨民，停止採買，又慮積貯無資。

translations.literal: Giving attention to storehouse reserves: one fears that selling at high prices harms the people, stopping state purchase, yet also fears lack of funds for accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: In strengthening storehouse reserves, one fears that selling grain at high prices harms the people if state purchases are stopped, yet also fears having no funds for accumulation.

sentences.zh: 詳加酌劑，擬請停戶部捐銀之例，令各省捐監於本地交納本色，以本地之穀實本地之倉，備本地之用。

translations.literal: After detailed weighing, he proposed stopping the Ministry of Revenue silver-donation precedent and ordering each province's purchase-degree donors to pay grain in kind locally, so local grain fills local granaries for local use.
translations.idiomatic: After careful deliberation, he proposed ending the Ministry of Revenue silver-donation precedent and requiring purchase-degree donors in each province to pay grain in kind locally, so that local grain would fill local granaries for local use.

sentences.zh: 不採買而倉儲自充，誠為兼濟之道。

translations.literal: Without state purchase, storehouse reserves would fill themselves—truly a way to aid both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Without state purchases, granary reserves would fill themselves—a truly balanced approach.

sentences.zh: 竊謂常平之積便於城，未甚便於鄉。

translations.literal: I privately consider that ever-normal granary stocks are convenient in cities but not very convenient in villages.
translations.idiomatic: I would observe that ever-normal granary stocks are convenient in cities but less so in villages.

sentences.zh: 城積多，則責之也專，而無能之吏或以為累；

translations.literal: If city stocks are many, responsibility is concentrated, and incapable officials may take it as a burden;
translations.idiomatic: When city stocks are large, responsibility falls on a few officials, and incompetent ones may treat it as a burden;

sentences.zh: 鄉積多，則守之者眾，而當社之民可以分勞。

translations.literal: If village stocks are many, there are many custodians, and the people of the community can share the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When village stocks are large, there are many custodians, and the people of each community can share the labor.

sentences.zh: 且社倉未有實際，以倉費無所出也。

translations.literal: Moreover community granaries have had no practical effect because there is no source for granary expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover community granaries have never worked in practice because there is no source of funds for their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 名有社倉，而倉不在社，社實無倉，往往然矣。

translations.literal: In name there are community granaries, yet the granary is not in the community, and the community in truth has no granary—this is often so.
translations.idiomatic: Community granaries exist in name only—the granary is not in the community, and the community in truth has no granary; this is often the case.

sentences.zh: 今捐穀多在於鄉，而例又議有倉費。

translations.literal: Now donated grain is mostly in villages, and regulations also provide for granary expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Donated grain is now mostly in villages, and regulations also provide for granary expenses.

sentences.zh: 擬請將此項捐納移入社倉，捐多則倉亦多。

translations.literal: He proposed shifting this donation into community granaries; more donation means more granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed redirecting these donations into community granaries; the more donated, the more granaries there would be.

sentences.zh: 取鄉保穀數而約舉之，大州縣八十堡，四堡一倉，倉一千二百五十石，總二萬五千石，中小州縣，以此類推。

translations.literal: Taking village baojia grain quotas and rounding up: large prefectures and counties have eighty forts, one granary per four forts, each granary one thousand two hundred fifty shi, totaling twenty-five thousand shi; medium and small prefectures and counties follow by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: Rounding up village baojia grain quotas: a large prefecture or county with eighty forts would have one granary per four forts, each holding one thousand two hundred fifty shi, for a total of twenty-five thousand shi; medium and small prefectures and counties would follow the same ratio.

sentences.zh: 儲蓄之方，莫便於此。

translations.literal: No method of storage is more convenient than this.
translations.idiomatic: No method of storage would be more convenient than this.

sentences.zh: 方今治平日久，一甲中不少良善，四堡之倉，輪推甲長遞管，互相稽覈，年清年款。

translations.literal: Now in a long period of peace, in every jia there are not a few good people; granaries of four forts should rotate stewardship among jia heads in succession, mutually auditing—accounts cleared each year.
translations.idiomatic: In this long era of peace, every jia has no shortage of upright men; granaries covering four forts could rotate stewardship among jia heads in turn, with mutual audits and annual settlement of accounts.

sentences.zh: 則社長累弊自除，而官考其成，隱然有上下相維之勢矣。」

translations.literal: Then the accumulated abuses of community heads would be removed of themselves, and when officials examine their performance there is tacitly a momentum of mutual support between upper and lower."
translations.idiomatic: The accumulated abuses of community heads would then disappear of themselves, and when officials review their performance there would tacitly be a structure of mutual support between upper and lower levels."

sentences.zh: 奏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor praised and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 十年，進喜雨詩四章，用其韻賜答。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he presented four rain-prayer poems; the emperor responded in matching rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he presented four poems celebrating rain; the emperor replied in matching rhyme.

sentences.zh: 京師錢貴，上令廷臣議平巿值，下各督撫仿行。

translations.literal: Copper cash was expensive in the capital; the emperor ordered court ministers to discuss stabilizing market prices and sent the plan down to governors for imitation.
translations.idiomatic: Copper cash had become expensive in the capital; the emperor ordered court ministers to discuss stabilizing market prices and sent the plan down to governors for implementation.

sentences.zh: 斯盛疏請視京師例，禁民間銅鋪毀錢；

translations.literal: Sisheng memorialized asking to follow the capital precedent and forbid private copper shops from destroying coins;
translations.idiomatic: Sisheng memorialized asking to follow the capital precedent and forbid private copper shops from melting down coins;

sentences.zh: 又令州縣每歲秋以平糶錢巿穀。

translations.literal: He also ordered prefectures and counties each autumn to use ever-normal funds to buy grain on the market.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered prefectures and counties each autumn to use ever-normal funds to purchase grain on the market.

sentences.zh: 時設局令商民以銀平易，又疏請捕私錢，並禁民私剪錢緣，兼限民間用銀二三兩以上、糶米二三石以上，皆不得以錢準銀，下廷臣議行。

translations.literal: At the time bureaus were set up ordering merchants and people to exchange silver at fair rates; he also memorialized asking to seize private coin, forbid people from privately clipping coin edges, and also limit that for private use of two or three taels of silver or more, or sale of two or three shi of rice or more, none may use cash to substitute for silver; this was sent down to court ministers for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus were then set up requiring merchants and commoners to exchange silver at fair rates; he also memorialized asking to seize illicit coin, forbid private clipping of coin edges, and require that transactions involving two or three taels of silver or more, or sales of two or three shi of rice or more, not be settled in cash at silver-equivalent rates; the proposal was sent to court ministers for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老請終養回籍。

translations.literal: Soon, because his mother was old, he asked to return home for full filial retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because his mother was elderly, he asked to return home for full filial retirement.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year.

sentences.zh: 斯盛著楚蒙山房易經解，唐鑑稱其「不廢像數而無技術曲說，不廢義理而無心性空談，在近日易家猶為篤實近理」雲。

translations.literal: Sisheng authored Chumeng Shanfang's Commentary on the Book of Changes; Tang Jian praised it: "It does not discard image-number methods yet has no technical forced interpretations; does not discard moral principle yet has no empty talk of mind-nature; among recent Yi scholars it remains solid and close to reason," he said.
translations.idiomatic: Sisheng authored the Chumeng Shanfang Commentary on the Book of Changes; Tang Jian praised it as "not discarding image-number methods yet free of technical forced interpretations; not discarding moral principle yet free of empty talk about mind-nature; among recent Yi scholars it remains solid and close to reason."

sentences.zh: =瑚寶=瑚寶，伊爾庫勒氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Hu Bao: Hu Bao, of the Irkule clan, a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bao, of the Irkule clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年武進士，授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he passed the military jinshi examination and was appointed third-rank imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign (1727) he passed the military jinshi examination and was appointed a third-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 補陝西永興堡守備。

translations.literal: He was appointed commandant of Yongxing Fort in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as commandant of Yongxing Fort in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 八年，準噶爾二萬餘犯科甚圖卡倫，從總兵樊廷進剿，遇於尖山，獲駝九十。

translations.literal: In the eighth year more than twenty thousand Dzungars violated Keshengtu kalawen; following Regional Commander Fan Ting in pursuit, he met them at Jianshan and captured ninety camels.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year more than twenty thousand Dzungars raided the Keshengtu kalawen; he joined Regional Commander Fan Ting in pursuit, met them at Jianshan, and captured ninety camels.

sentences.zh: 又進敗之於北山，又遇於烏素達阪，擊之退。

translations.literal: Advancing further he defeated them at Beishan; meeting them again at Wusudaban, he attacked and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing further he defeated them at Beishan; meeting them again at Wusudaban Pass, he attacked and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 翌日，分七隊迎戰，瑚寶督兵奮擊，自辰至申，至科甚圖，殪敵無算。

translations.literal: The next day, dividing into seven columns to meet battle, Hu Bao supervised the troops in fierce attack from the chen hour to the shen hour, reaching Keshengtu and killing countless enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he divided his forces into seven columns to meet the enemy; Hu Bao led the troops in fierce attack from morning until mid-afternoon, reaching Keshengtu and killing countless enemies.

sentences.zh: 敵圍峨崙磯，瑚寶赴援，乘夜來襲，領先鋒轉戰雪中七晝夜，奪波羅磚並白墩、紅山、鏡兒泉諸地，得其渠六，敵潰遁。

translations.literal: The enemy besieged E'kunji; Hu Bao went to relieve them, taking advantage of night to attack; leading the vanguard he fought in snow for seven days and nights, seizing Boluozhuan together with Baidun, Hongshan, Jing'erquan, and other places, capturing six of their chiefs; the enemy broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy besieged E'kunji, Hu Bao went to the rescue and attacked by night; leading the vanguard he fought in snow for seven days and nights, seizing Boluozhuan along with Baidun, Hongshan, Jing'erquan, and other places, capturing six of their chiefs before the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 九年，準噶爾复犯吐魯番，瑚寶從廷進剿，以勞賜白金三百。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Dzungars again violated Turfan; Hu Bao followed Ting in pursuit and was rewarded with three hundred taels of silver for his labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Dzungars again raided Turfan; Hu Bao joined Fan Ting in pursuit and was rewarded with three hundred taels of silver for his service.

sentences.zh: 累遷肅州鎮右營游擊。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to mobile brigade commander of the Right Battalion of Suzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to mobile brigade commander of the Right Battalion of Suzhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，复累遷山西大同總兵，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he was again repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Datong in Shanxi and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he was promoted again to regional commander of Datong in Shanxi and granted a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年，遷固原提督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Qianlong he was transferred to be regional commander of Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Qianlong reign, he was appointed regional commander of Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「固原兵驕縱，犯上不法。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him, saying: "The soldiers at Guyuan are arrogant and unruly, disrespectful toward superiors and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "The troops at Guyuan have grown proud and insubordinate; they defy their superiors and break the law.

sentences.zh: 瑚寶當加意整飭，使兵知畏法，漸次轉移。」

translations.literal: Hu Bao must give special attention to rectifying and disciplining them, so that the soldiers learn to fear the law and their habits gradually change."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bao must take pains to tighten discipline so the soldiers learn to respect the law and their conduct gradually improves.

sentences.zh: 又諭之曰：「固原城內外兵多民少，回民過半，私立掌教等名。

translations.literal: He also instructed him, saying: "Inside and outside Guyuan city soldiers outnumber civilians, more than half are Hui people, and there are privately established posts such as teaching chief.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Within and around Guyuan, soldiers outnumber civilians; Hui people make up more than half the population, and unauthorized titles such as teaching chief have been established in private.

sentences.zh: 應時時體訪，期杜釁端。

translations.literal: He should continually inquire in person, hoping to cut off the beginnings of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: You must investigate this regularly to prevent trouble before it starts.

sentences.zh: 回人充標兵，應留意分別：豪悍者懲黜，怯弱者淘汰，使營伍肅清。」

translations.literal: Among Hui people who serve as standard-bearer soldiers, he should pay attention to distinguishing them: the overbearing and fierce should be punished and dismissed, the timid and weak should be weeded out, so that the camps become clean and orderly."
translations.idiomatic: Among the Hui serving as garrison soldiers, take care to sort them out: punish and remove the bold and violent, weed out the timid and weak, and clear the ranks.

sentences.zh: 旋疏請營兵具互結，以弓箭、鳥槍、技藝三項輪操；

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he memorialized requesting that camp soldiers form mutual-guarantee groups and take turns at drill in archery, muskets, and martial skills;
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he submitted a memorial asking that garrison troops form mutual-guarantee groups and rotate training in archery, firearms, and martial skills;

sentences.zh: 冬季借支春餉，次年四季扣除。

translations.literal: in winter advance payment of the spring ration could be drawn, to be deducted in four installments over the following year.
translations.idiomatic: with spring rations advanced in winter and repaid in four installments over the following year.

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved it for implementation.

sentences.zh: 師徵金川，調固原步兵二千。

translations.literal: When the army marched to subjugate Jinchuan, two thousand Guyuan infantrymen were mobilized.
translations.idiomatic: For the campaign against Jinchuan, two thousand infantry from Guyuan were called up.

sentences.zh: 瑚寶請馱載軍裝，以二騾代三馬，可省費三分一，從之。

translations.literal: Hu Bao requested pack transport for military equipment, replacing three horses with two mules, which could save one-third of the expense; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bao proposed carrying army gear on pack animals, using two mules instead of three horses to cut costs by a third; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，署甘肅巡撫，兼辦總督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he served as acting governor of Gansu and concurrently handled the duties of governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he served as acting governor of Gansu while also handling the governor-general's affairs.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「陝西歉收，師行採買草料為難。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Shaanxi had a poor harvest, and it is difficult for the army on the march to purchase forage and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Shaanxi's harvest fell short, making it hard for marching troops to buy forage.

sentences.zh: 將甘肅倉貯豆石撥用，俟兵過照買還倉。」

translations.literal: He proposed to allocate beans and grain stored in Gansu granaries for use, and after the army passed through to buy and return them to the granaries according to purchase."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed drawing on Gansu's stored grain and beans and replacing the stock once the army had passed through.

sentences.zh: 上以通融協濟，有益軍需，溫諭嘉勉。

translations.literal: The emperor, deeming this flexible mutual aid beneficial to military supplies, warmly instructed him with praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this flexible arrangement as a help to the army's supply needs and sent him warm words of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 召授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋署陝甘總督，調湖廣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu and was transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu, then was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 又改授漕運總督。

translations.literal: He was then reassigned as Grain Transport Governor-General.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Grain Transport Governor-General instead.

sentences.zh: 坐失察盧魯生偽造奏稿事，奪官，仍留任。

translations.literal: On account of failure to detect Lu Lusheng's forgery of a memorial draft, he was stripped of rank but retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his rank for failing to detect Lu Lusheng's forged memorial draft but was allowed to remain in his post.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，諡恭恪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, and was given the posthumous title Gongke.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after and was posthumously honored with the title Gongke ("Respectful and Diligent").

sentences.zh: =衛哲治=衛哲治，字我愚，河南濟源人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhezhi: Wei Zhezhi, courtesy name Woyu, a native of Jiyuan in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhezhi, courtesy name Woyu, was a native of Jiyuan in Henan.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，以拔貢生廷試優等，發江南委用。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng, as a selected tribute student he ranked among the superior in the palace examination and was dispatched to Jiangnan for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Yongzheng reign, having ranked among the top tribute students in the palace examination, he was sent to Jiangnan for official service.

sentences.zh: 初署贛榆知縣，調鹽城。

translations.literal: He was first appointed acting magistrate of Ganyu and was then transferred to Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He began as acting magistrate of Ganyu before being transferred to Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 值蝗災，設六條拊循：優禮德望，饋餉高年，旌獎孝義，經理煢獨，譏警遊惰，約束過犯。

translations.literal: When a locust disaster struck, he established six measures for relief and conciliation: honoring men of virtue and standing, supplying provisions to the elderly, commending filial piety and righteousness, caring for the orphaned and alone, admonishing idlers and the lazy, and restraining offenders.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts devastated the county, he instituted six relief measures: honoring men of local standing, feeding the aged, rewarding the filial and righteous, tending the orphaned and destitute, reproving idlers, and restraining wrongdoers.

sentences.zh: 縣北有司河，匯上游七縣水入海。

translations.literal: North of the county was the Si River, which collected the waters of seven upstream counties and discharged them into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: North of the county ran the Si River, channeling water from seven upstream counties out to sea.

sentences.zh: 夏旱水弱，海潮至，咸苦不可食，甚乃浸溢民田；

translations.literal: In summer drought the water ran weak, sea tides arrived, the water turned salty and bitter and was undrinkable, and in severe cases even flooded and overflowed onto people's fields;
translations.idiomatic: In summer drought the river ran low; when the tide came in the water turned brackish and undrinkable, and in the worst cases flooded the farmland;

sentences.zh: 秋水盛，又患河寬流緩，入海不速。

translations.literal: in autumn when the water was abundant, the concern was again that the river was wide and the flow slow, so discharge into the sea was not swift.
translations.idiomatic: in autumn, when the water ran high, the wide sluggish channel could not carry it quickly to the sea.

sentences.zh: 哲治建閘立斗門，蓄洩有備。

translations.literal: Zhezhi built sluice gates and erected sluice doors, so that storage and release were both provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezhi built locks and sluice gates so water could be stored and released as needed.

sentences.zh: 斥鹵化膏腴，歲有涸出地，給無業民承耕。

translations.literal: Saline land was transformed into fertile soil; each year land that dried out became available and was given to landless people to take up cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Saline ground was reclaimed into rich farmland, and each year newly dried land was allotted to landless peasants to farm.

sentences.zh: 田沉沒而糧未除者，悉請豁免。

translations.literal: For fields submerged while grain tax had not yet been removed, he memorialized requesting complete exemption.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for full remission of grain tax on fields that had been flooded but were still on the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 循海築土墩九十餘，潮大，漁者得就墩逃溺，號「救命墩」。

translations.literal: Along the coast he built more than ninety earthen mounds; when tides were high fishermen could flee to the mounds to escape drowning, and they called them "life-saving mounds."
translations.idiomatic: He built more than ninety earthen mounds along the coast; when tides surged, fishermen could climb them to escape drowning—they came to be called "life-saving mounds."

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，補長洲，兼攝吳縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong he was appointed to Changzhou and concurrently administered Wuxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianlong he was appointed magistrate of Changzhou and also took charge of Wuxian.

sentences.zh: 請豁坍荒逋賦十餘萬。

translations.literal: He requested exemption of more than one hundred thousand taels of arrear taxes on collapsed and wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: He secured remission of more than one hundred thousand taels in unpaid taxes on collapsed and abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷海州知州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to be prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲歉治賑，全活二十萬人，流民有自山東就食者。

translations.literal: In a year of poor harvest he organized relief and saved two hundred thousand people; there were also displaced people who came from Shandong seeking food.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he organized relief that saved two hundred thousand lives, including refugees from Shandong who had come seeking food.

sentences.zh: 擢淮安知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to be prefect of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 十年，河決陳家堡，漂溺男女、田廬無算。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Yellow River broke at Chenjiabao, drowning men and women and sweeping away fields and dwellings without number.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Yellow River breached at Chenjiabao, drowning countless people and sweeping away farms and homes.

sentences.zh: 哲治遣小舟載餅餌救之，躬涉風濤，往來存問。

translations.literal: Zhezhi sent small boats carrying cakes and food to rescue them, personally wading through wind and waves and going back and forth to inquire after survivors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezhi sent small boats loaded with food to the rescue and waded through the surging floodwaters himself, going back and forth to comfort survivors.

sentences.zh: 山東复災，流民南下。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered disaster again, and displaced people moved south.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong was stricken again, and refugees moved southward.

sentences.zh: 哲治捐俸，益以勸募，葺草屋，自清江浦屬魚溝以北，銜接二百餘裡，所在給粥糜、衣、藥。

translations.literal: Zhezhi contributed his salary, supplemented by solicited donations, built thatched huts, and from Qingjiangpu north through Yugou in continuous stretches of more than two hundred li, everywhere provided gruel, clothing, and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezhi donated his salary, raised more by public appeal, and built thatched shelters; for more than two hundred li north from Qingjiangpu through Yugou, he provided gruel, clothing, and medicine at stations along the route.

sentences.zh: 十三年，山東又災，兩江總督尹繼善令哲治運賑米至台莊。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Shandong was disaster-stricken again; Liangjiang governor-general Yin Jishan ordered Zhezhi to transport relief grain to Taizhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Shandong was hit again, Liangjiang governor-general Yin Jishan ordered Zhezhi to ship relief grain to Taizhuang.

sentences.zh: 上聞哲治善治賑，調山東登萊青道。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing that Zhezhi was skilled at organizing famine relief, transferred him to the Deng-Lai-Qing circuit of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of Zhezhi's skill at famine relief, he transferred him to the Deng-Lai-Qing circuit in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 居數月，擢布政使。

translations.literal: After several months he was promoted to financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed to be governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「歙縣馬田地在休寧，請折徵充餉。」

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "The horse-land fields of She County are located in Xiuning; I request that they be commuted to cash payment for provisioning."
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "She County's horse-land tax plots lie in Xiuning; I request they be converted to cash levies for military provisioning.

sentences.zh: 又言：「廣德催糧，每圖有單頭，數圖有經催。

translations.literal: He also said: "In Guangde, when pressing for grain tax, each tu had a dan tou, and several tu had a jing cui.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "In Guangde's grain collection, each tu had a lead collector and several tu shared a supervising collector.

sentences.zh: 前巡撫潘思榘改行順莊，轉有未便，請得仍舊。」

translations.literal: The former governor Pan Simo changed to the shun zhuang method, which in turn proved inconvenient; I request that the old system be restored."
translations.idiomatic: Former governor Pan Simo had switched to the shun zhuang method, which proved impractical; I ask that the former practice be restored.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved by the ministries.

sentences.zh: 旋召詣京師。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十五年，令回任，上諭之曰：「汝不滿朕意。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was ordered back to his post; the emperor instructed him, saying: "You do not satisfy my intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was sent back to his post; the emperor told him: "You have disappointed me.

sentences.zh: 以一時無人，故仍留汝。

translations.literal: Because for the moment there is no one else, I still keep you in place.
translations.idiomatic: For lack of anyone else at the moment, I am keeping you on.

sentences.zh: 宜奮勉改過。」

translations.literal: You ought to exert yourself and reform your faults."
translations.idiomatic: You should apply yourself and mend your ways.

sentences.zh: 調廣西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 入覲，哲治具言親老不便迎養，命仍留安徽。

translations.literal: When he had audience, Zhezhi fully explained that his parents were elderly and it was inconvenient to bring them for support; he was ordered to remain in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: At audience, Zhezhi explained that his aged parents made it hard for him to move; he was ordered to stay in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 尋丁憂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went into mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，服闋，署兵部侍郎，暫管戶部事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when mourning ended, he served as acting vice president of the Ministry of War and temporarily handled the affairs of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, after mourning, he served as acting vice minister of war and temporarily managed revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 复授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: He was again appointed to be governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 疏建歙縣惠濟倉。

translations.literal: He memorialized to build the Huiji Granary in She County.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for the construction of the Huiji relief granary in She County.

sentences.zh: 再調廣西。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guangxi again.

sentences.zh: 二十年，內擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted from within to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 因病乞回籍。

translations.literal: On account of illness he requested to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Ill health led him to request retirement to his home province.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-first year.

sentences.zh: =蘇昌=蘇昌，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正藍旗人，滿丕孫。

translations.literal: Su Chang: Su Chang, of the Irgen Gioro clan, a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner, grandson of Manpi.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner and grandson of Manpi.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十九年，自監生考取內閣中書，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year of Kangxi, from the status of purchased student he passed examination for secretary of the Grand Secretariat and was transferred to reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year of Kangxi, having entered through the purchased-student route, he passed the examination for Grand Secretariat secretary and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 考選浙江道御史。

translations.literal: By competitive selection he was appointed censor of the Zhejiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected censor of the Zhejiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，命巡察吉林。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was ordered to inspect Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he was assigned to inspect Jilin.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「船廠、寧古塔、三姓、白都訥、阿爾楚喀等處滿官不知律例，訟案稽延累民，請自京師遣官往理。」

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "At Chuan Chang, Ningguta, Sanxing, Baidun, Aerchuka, and other places Manchu officials do not know statutes and precedents; litigation cases drag on and burden the people; I request that officials be dispatched from the capital to handle them."
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "At Shipyard, Ningguta, Sanxing, Baidun, A'erchuka, and other posts, Manchu officials are unfamiliar with law; lawsuits linger and burden the people—I request sending officials from the capital to adjudicate.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made supervising secretary of the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 屢擢至奉天府尹。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he reached the post of prefect of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated promotions he rose to prefect of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 十一年，奉天被水，蘇昌請設廠四鄉，增辦賑官吏公費；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Fengtian was inundated; Su Chang requested establishing relief stations in the four rural districts and increasing official expenses for famine administration;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when floods struck Fengtian, Su Chang proposed relief stations in the four rural districts and increased allowances for relief officials;

sentences.zh: 又請禁止遊民往來奉天等處。

translations.literal: he also requested prohibiting vagrants from traveling back and forth to Fengtian and other places.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked that itinerants be barred from moving freely into Fengtian and neighboring areas.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to be governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十六年，署兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he served as acting governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he served as acting governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫舒輅請於思陵土州沿邊種竻竹，杜私越；

translations.literal: Guangxi governor Shu Ge requested planting rattan bamboo along the border of Siling Tuzhou to block unauthorized crossing;
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi governor Shu Ge proposed planting rattan bamboo along the Siling Tuzhou frontier to stop illegal crossings;

sentences.zh: 土目因以侵夷地致釁。

translations.literal: native chieftains thereby encroached on Yi territory and provoked clashes.
translations.idiomatic: but native headmen used the scheme to encroach on tribal lands and provoke conflict.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌奏：「鎮安、太平、南寧等沿邊二千餘裡，無論種竹難遍。

translations.literal: Su Chang memorialized: "Along more than two thousand li of the border of Zhen'an, Taiping, Nanning, and other places, it is in any case difficult to plant bamboo everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang argued: "Along more than two thousand li of frontier in Zhen'an, Taiping, Nanning, and elsewhere, bamboo cannot be planted everywhere in any case.

sentences.zh: 料理稍疏，事端轉啟，請更正。」

translations.literal: If management is even slightly lax, incidents will instead arise; I request that the matter be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: Any slack enforcement will only stir up trouble; I ask that the policy be reversed.

sentences.zh: 上責舒輅輕率，寢其事。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Shu Ge for rashness and shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Shu Ge for recklessness and dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌奏：「瓊州海外瘠區，貧民生計艱難，有可墾荒地二百五十餘頃，請招民開墾，免其昇科。」

translations.literal: Su Chang memorialized: "Qiongzhou is an impoverished region beyond the sea; the livelihood of the poor is hard; there is reclaimable wasteland of more than two hundred fifty qing; I request recruiting people to open it for cultivation and exempting it from upgraded tax assessment."
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang reported: "Qiongzhou is a poor outlying region where peasants scrape to live; more than 250 qing of wasteland could be reclaimed—I ask that settlers be recruited and the land exempted from upgraded taxation.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 召來京。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed vice president of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，署工部尚書，授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he served as acting Minister of Works and was appointed governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he served briefly as Minister of Works before being appointed governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 在籍御史孫紹基稱與按察使沈作朋舊為同官，因以取賕。

translations.literal: Censor on leave Sun Shaoji claimed he had formerly been colleagues with provincial judicial commissioner Shen Zuopeng and had taken bribes on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Sun Shaoji, on leave in his home province, admitted he had taken bribes from provincial judicial commissioner Shen Zuopeng, with whom he had once served.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌劾奏抵罪，並請定回籍之員與有司交結處分。

translations.literal: Su Chang impeached and memorialized for punishment, and also requested fixing penalties for officials on leave in their home provinces who associate with local administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang impeached both men and called for fixed penalties against officials on home leave who collude with local magistrates.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌劾湖北巡撫週琬乖張掩飾，上調蘇昌兩廣，命繼任總督愛必達察琬。

translations.literal: Su Chang impeached Huguang governor Zhou Wan for perverse conduct and cover-ups; the emperor transferred Su Chang to the Two Guangs and ordered his successor as governor-general, Aibida, to investigate Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang impeached Huguang governor Zhou Wan for stubborn obstruction and concealment; the emperor moved Su Chang to the Two Guangs and ordered his successor Aibida to investigate Zhou.

sentences.zh: 愛必達發琬匿災徇劣吏狀，奪官，戍巴里坤。

translations.literal: Aibida exposed Wan's concealment of disasters and indulgence of inferior officials; Wan was stripped of rank and exiled to Barkol.
translations.idiomatic: Aibida uncovered Zhou's concealment of famine and favoritism toward corrupt subordinates; Zhou was dismissed and exiled to Barkol.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌至廣東，又劾碣石總兵王陳榮貪黷，奪官，論如律。

translations.literal: When Su Chang reached Guangdong, he again impeached regional commander Wang Chenrong of Jieshi for greed and corruption; Chenrong was stripped of rank and sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Guangdong, Su Chang also impeached Jieshi regional commander Wang Chenrong for corruption; Wang was stripped of rank and sentenced under law.

sentences.zh: 加蘇昌太子太保。

translations.literal: Su Chang was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，奏言：「廣東產米不敷民食，宜多貯社穀，以補常平不足。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he memorialized, saying: "Guangdong's rice production does not suffice for the people's food; it is appropriate to store more community grain to supplement the insufficiency of changping reserves.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he reported: "Guangdong does not grow enough rice to feed its people; more community grain should be stored to supplement the regular granaries.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後息穀統存州縣備賑，免其變價。」

translations.literal: I request that henceforth interest grain be stored entirely at the prefecture and county level for relief reserves, exempting it from being sold at market price."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed keeping all granary interest grain in county stores for famine relief instead of selling it.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 調閩浙總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 在兩廣薦鹽運使王概，概以贓敗，下吏議。

translations.literal: While in the Two Guangs he had recommended salt transport commissioner Wang Gai; Gai was exposed for bribery and handed over to officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Two Guangs he had recommended salt transport commissioner Wang Gai, who was later caught for corruption and referred for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 御史羅暹春因劾蘇昌瞻徇糊塗，不堪節制海疆。

translations.literal: Censor Luo Xianchun thereupon impeached Su Chang for favoritism and muddle-headedness, unfit to command the maritime frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Luo Xianchun then impeached Su Chang for favoritism and incompetence, declaring him unfit to govern the coastal provinces.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「蘇昌不能辭失察之咎。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Su Chang cannot escape blame for failure to detect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Su Chang cannot escape censure for lack of oversight.

sentences.zh: 節制海疆，乃朕所簡用，非御史所宜言。」

translations.literal: Command of the maritime frontier is what I myself select and appoint; it is not for censors to speak of inappropriately."
translations.idiomatic: Governing the coast is my appointee's charge—not something a censor may second-guess.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌別疏劾知縣劉紹汜，下刑部。

translations.literal: Su Chang separately memorialized impeaching magistrate Liu Shaoxu, and the case was sent to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang separately impeached magistrate Liu Shaoxu, and the case went to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 上以暹春與紹汜同為江西人，疑暹春劾蘇昌為紹汜地，詰責暹春，改主事；

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xianchun and Shaoxu were both natives of Jiangxi, suspected Xianchun impeached Su Chang to make room for Shaoxu; he reprimanded Xianchun and reduced him to secretary;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that Luo and Liu were both Jiangxi natives and suspected Luo had attacked Su to shield Liu; he rebuked Luo and demoted him to secretary;

sentences.zh: 命蘇昌留任。

translations.literal: he ordered Su Chang to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang was ordered to remain in his post.

sentences.zh: 三十年，台灣淡水生番為亂，焚鱟殼莊，民死者五十餘。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, raw aborigines in Tamsui, Taiwan, rose in rebellion, burned Houshell Village, and more than fifty civilians died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, unpacified aborigines in Tamsui, Taiwan, rebelled, burned Houshell Village, and killed more than fifty common people.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌檄按察使余文儀會台灣總兵督兵討平之。

translations.literal: Su Chang dispatched a summons to Provincial Judicial Commissioner Yu Wenyi to join the Taiwan regional commander in supervising troops to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang ordered Provincial Judicial Commissioner Yu Wenyi to join the Taiwan regional commander in raising troops to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，入覲。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, he came to court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year, he traveled to court for an audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡恪勤。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Keqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Keqin, "Respectful and Diligent."

sentences.zh: 子富綱，官雲貴總督。

translations.literal: His son Fugang served as governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fugang rose to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌在兩廣，有巨室橫斃人母，誣其子，獄久具，勾決本已下。

translations.literal: While Su Chang was in Guangdong and Guangxi, a great house tyrannically killed a man's mother and falsely accused the son; the case had long been concluded, and the execution warrant had already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Chang's tenure in the Two Guangs, a powerful family had murdered a man's mother but framed the son; the case had long since been decided, and the execution order was already on its way down.

sentences.zh: 蘇昌疑其冤，親鞫之，得實，疏自劾，上獎諭之，寘知縣於法，時論稱焉。

translations.literal: Su Chang suspected a miscarriage of justice, personally tried the case, got at the truth, memorialized impeaching himself, the emperor praised and instructed him, the county magistrate was punished according to law, and public opinion praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang suspected wrongful conviction, tried the case himself, and uncovered the truth. He memorialized to impeach himself; the emperor commended him, the magistrate was punished by law, and contemporaries praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: =鶴年=鶴年，字芝仙，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: He Nian: He Nian, courtesy name Zhixian, of the Irgen Gioro clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He Nian, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner; his courtesy name was Zhixian.

sentences.zh: 父春山，康熙五十一年進士，選庶吉士，官至盛京兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Chunshan passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-first year of Kangxi, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and rose to vice minister of the Board of War at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chunshan earned jinshi in the fifty-first year of Kangxi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and eventually became vice minister of the Board of War at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 鶴年，乾隆元年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，兼公中佐領。

translations.literal: He Nian passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Qianlong, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, was appointed reviser, and concurrently served as company commander of the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He Nian took jinshi in the first year of Qianlong, joined the Hanlin as a bachelor, was made a reviser, and also held a company command in the garrison banner.

sentences.zh: 三遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became a Grand Secretariat chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions, he became a Grand Secretariat scholar.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was promoted to vice minister in charge of the granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, he was promoted to vice minister of the imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 以京師米貴，疏請京、通俸餉米先半月支放。

translations.literal: Because rice in the capital was dear, he memorialized requesting that salary grain for Beijing and Tongzhou be disbursed a half month early.
translations.idiomatic: With grain prices soaring in the capital, he asked that salary rice for Beijing and Tongzhou be paid out half a month ahead of schedule.

sentences.zh: 十八年，劾坐糧廳郎中綽克托剛愎自用，遲延徇縱，綽克托坐奪官。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he impeached Director of the Grain Transport Bureau Lang Clerk Chuoketuo for stubborn self-will, delay, and indulgent laxity; Chuoketuo was stripped of his office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, he impeached Chuoketuo, director at the grain transport bureau, for obstinacy and lax supervision; Chuoketuo was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「通州南倉建自明天順間，後併入中倉。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The South Granary at Tongzhou was built in the Tianshun reign of the Ming; later it was merged into the Central Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported: "Tongzhou's South Granary was built during the Ming Tianshun reign and later merged into the Central Granary.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，復分為二，與西倉分貯漕白米。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period it was again divided in two, and together with the West Granary it separately stored tribute canal white rice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng it was split in two again, sharing storage of white tribute rice with the West Granary.

sentences.zh: 臣見中西倉足敷收貯，請裁南倉歸併中西倉。」

translations.literal: Your minister sees that the Central and West Granaries suffice for storage; I request abolishing the South Granary and merging it into the Central and West Granaries."
translations.idiomatic: I find the Central and West Granaries adequate for storage and ask that the South Granary be abolished and folded into them.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, he was appointed governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, he was made governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 奏陳平米價，嚴保甲，緝竊盜案，禁私鑄、私雕諸事。

translations.literal: He memorialized stating fixed rates per mu of land tax, strict enforcement of the mutual-responsibility system, pursuit of theft cases, and prohibition of private coining and private engraving, among other matters.
translations.idiomatic: He reported on fixed land-tax rates, tightened the mutual-responsibility system, cracked down on theft, and banned illegal minting and engraving.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「諸凡行之以實，持之以久。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed, saying: "In all these matters, carry them out in earnest and sustain them over time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Put all of this into practice in earnest, and keep at it without slackening.

sentences.zh: 勉之！」

translations.literal: Encourage yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Press on!

sentences.zh: 尋复疏請以化州石城官租穀碾給海安營兵米。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again memorialized requesting that official rent grain from Shicheng in Huazhou be milled and supplied as soldiers' rice to the Haian garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he asked that official rent grain from Shicheng in Huazhou be milled and issued as rations to the Haian garrison.

sentences.zh: 又奏海陽蔡家園土堤改築灰牆，出俸倡修。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that the earthen dike at Caijiayuan in Haiyang should be rebuilt as a lime wall, and he took the lead in repair by contributing from his salary.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed rebuilding the earthen embankment at Caijiayuan in Haiyang as a lime wall, donating his own salary to start the work.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，奏言：「番禺、花、陽春諸縣徵收兵米，有所謂廚房米、官眷米，相傳起於明代籓府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he memorialized, saying: "Panyu, Hua, and Yangchun counties and others collect soldiers' rice, including what are called kitchen rice and officials' dependents' rice, said to originate from princely establishments of the Ming dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, he reported that Panyu, Hua, Yangchun, and other counties were levying troops' rice—including "kitchen rice" and "dependents' rice"—traditions said to date from Ming princely establishments.

sentences.zh: 後為旗營武職俸米，凡萬二千餘石，必細長潔白，產少價昂，甚為民累，應請禁革。」

translations.literal: Later they became salary rice for banner military officers, totaling more than twelve thousand shi; it had to be slender, long, clean, and white—scarce in supply and high in price, a great burden on the people, and should be requested forbidden and abolished."
translations.idiomatic: They had become salary rice for banner officers—more than 12,000 shi in all—and had to be slender, long, clean, and white; scarce and costly, they weighed heavily on the people and ought to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the proposal.

sentences.zh: 調山東巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 奏言濟寧、魚台、金鄉、滕、嶧諸州縣積水為災，上命加意賑恤。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Jining, Yutai, Jinxiang, Teng, and Yi prefectures and counties had standing floodwater and suffered disaster; the emperor ordered special care in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting floods in Jining, Yutai, Jinxiang, Teng, Yi, and other districts, he received orders to give the affected areas exceptional relief.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上南巡，迎蹕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when the emperor made a southern tour, he welcomed the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, he welcomed the emperor's procession during the southern tour.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「海豐地處海濱，東北鄉尤低下，易罹水患。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Haifeng lies on the coast; the northeastern townships are especially low and easily suffer flooding.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Haifeng stood on the coast, its northeastern districts especially low and flood-prone.

sentences.zh: 積年逋賦請豁免，乾隆十一年至二十年舊欠並改用下則。」

translations.literal: He requested exemption of accumulated years of arrears in tax payment, and that old debts from the eleventh to the twentieth year of Qianlong be converted to the lower tax grade."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that arrears be forgiven and old debts from Qianlong 11–20 reassessed at the lower tax rate.

sentences.zh: 復奏濟寧等五州縣積水尚未盡涸。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that in Jining and the other five prefectures and counties the standing water had not yet fully drained away.
translations.idiomatic: He added that standing water still had not fully receded in Jining and four other districts.

sentences.zh: 上以江南宿虹、靈壁，河南永城、夏邑，皆有積水，命侍郎裘曰修會諸督撫籌度疏消。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Su and Hong in Jiangnan, and Lingbi, and Henan's Yongcheng and Xiayi all had standing water, ordered Vice Minister Qiu Yuexiu to join the various governors-general and governors in planning drainage.
translations.idiomatic: Noting standing water as well in Su and Hong in Jiangnan, Lingbi, and Yongcheng and Xiayi in Henan, the emperor sent Vice Minister Qiu Yuexiu to work with the provincial governors on drainage plans.

sentences.zh: 七月，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, he was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 奏：「東省水患頻仍，正與裘曰修商度，擬濬伊家河，洩微山湖水。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Disasters from water have been frequent in the eastern province; I am currently consulting with Qiu Yuexiu and plan to dredge the Yijia River to discharge water from Weishan Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Floods have struck Shandong again and again; I am working with Qiu Yuexiu to dredge the Yijia River and drain Weishan Lake.

sentences.zh: 河自韓莊迤西至江南梁旺城入運河，計程七十里，需銀十三四萬，一切正須經理。

translations.literal: The river runs from Han Village westward to Liangwangcheng in Jiangnan where it enters the Grand Canal, a distance of seventy li, requiring one hundred thirty to forty thousand taels of silver; all of this urgently needs to be managed.
translations.idiomatic: The channel would run seventy li from Han Village west to Liangwangcheng in Jiangnan, where it joins the Grand Canal—costing 130,000–140,000 taels—and everything must be overseen at once.

sentences.zh: 又與河臣張師載商濬運河，並及建堤。

translations.literal: He also consulted with Canal Director Zhang Shizai on dredging the Grand Canal, including building dikes.
translations.idiomatic: He was also planning with Canal Director Zhang Shizai to dredge the Grand Canal and build embankments.

sentences.zh: 事不容已，懇留任督辦。」

translations.literal: The matter brooks no delay; he earnestly requested to remain in post to supervise and handle it."
translations.idiomatic: The work could not wait, and he begged to stay on and supervise it.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「覽奏，具見良心。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed, saying: "Reading your memorial, I fully see your conscientiousness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Your memorial shows genuine conscientiousness.

sentences.zh: 然朕以無人，不得不用汝。

translations.literal: Yet because I have no one else, I cannot but use you.
translations.idiomatic: But I have no one else for the post, so I must still use you.

sentences.zh: 汝仍遵前命。」

translations.literal: You must still follow the previous order."
translations.idiomatic: You must still proceed as originally ordered."

sentences.zh: 十月，復命以總督銜管山東巡撫事，綜理工程。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he was again ordered to manage Shandong governor affairs with governor-general rank and oversee the engineering projects in general.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, he was reassigned to handle the governor's duties in Shandong under governor-general rank and to oversee the works as a whole.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「濬運河必先濬伊家河以洩積水，使久淹地畝漸次涸出，然後履勘估修，庶工實費省。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Dredging the Grand Canal must begin with dredging the Yijia River to discharge accumulated water, so that long-flooded fields gradually dry out; only then should on-site surveys and repair estimates be made, so that labor and expenses may be saved.
translations.idiomatic: He argued: "The Grand Canal can be dredged only after the Yijia River is opened to drain the standing water, letting long-submerged fields dry out step by step; repairs should then be surveyed and estimated on the ground, saving labor and cost.

sentences.zh: 請俟春暖鳩工，不致有誤新運。」

translations.literal: I request waiting until spring warmth to mobilize labor, so as not to disrupt the new grain transport."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to wait until warm weather in spring to start work, so the new transport season would not be disrupted.

sentences.zh: 又偕師載疏言：「運河淤墊日甚，尋常修濬，非經久之策。

translations.literal: He also joined Zhang Shizai in memorializing, saying: "Silting of the Grand Canal grows worse daily; ordinary dredging is not a lasting policy.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Shizai added: "The Grand Canal is silting up faster every day; routine dredging is no long-term solution.

sentences.zh: 應自濟寧石佛閘起北至臨清閘，逐一探底，以深八尺為度，俾河身一體平坦。」

translations.literal: From Shifo Sluice at Jining northward to Linqing Sluice, the bottom should be probed section by section, with eight chi of depth as the standard, so that the river channel becomes uniformly level."
translations.idiomatic: From Shifo Sluice at Jining north to Linqing Sluice, the bed should be sounded section by section to a uniform depth of eight chi, making the channel level throughout.

sentences.zh: 上韙其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，伊家河工竟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Yijia River project was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, work on the Yijia River was finished.

sentences.zh: 又奏言：「運河淤淺處分段築壩，測量纖路，多民居。

translations.literal: He again memorialized, saying: "At shallow, silted sections of the Grand Canal, dams were to be built by segments and the towpath measured; there were many dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: He further reported: "Where the canal had shoaled, dams were to be built in sections and the towpath surveyed—areas thick with homes.

sentences.zh: 草土屋原售，給價拆除；

translations.literal: For thatched and earthen houses whose owners were willing to sell, compensation was given and they were demolished;
translations.idiomatic: Owners willing to sell thatched or mud houses were paid and the buildings removed;

sentences.zh: 瓦屋不原售，量將纖路加寬。

translations.literal: for tile-roofed houses whose owners were unwilling to sell, the towpath was to be widened as measured.
translations.idiomatic: where tile-roofed houses could not be bought, the towpath was widened as needed instead.

sentences.zh: 被水民田速為疏消，俾為種麥；

translations.literal: flooded civilian fields were to be drained quickly so that wheat could be planted;
translations.idiomatic: flooded farmland was to be drained quickly so peasants could sow wheat;

sentences.zh: 應修橋樑，察有解江餘石應用，不使估報買採。」

translations.literal: bridges needing repair should use leftover stone from the Jie River project where available, and not allow inflated estimates for purchase and quarrying."
translations.idiomatic: for bridges under repair, leftover stone from the Jie River works should be used where possible, with no padded purchase estimates.

sentences.zh: 上以「實心經理，不負任使」嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him with the words "conscientious in management, not failing the commission entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him for "managing affairs with genuine dedication and living up to the trust placed in him."

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子太保、兵部尚書銜，祀賢良祠，賜祭葬，諡文勤。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the rank of minister of the Board of War, enshrined in the Temple of Worthies, granted funeral honors, posthumous title Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with minister-of-war rank, entered in the Temple of Worthies, granted state funeral honors, and given the posthumous name Wenqin, "Cultivated and Diligent."

sentences.zh: 子桂林，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Guilin has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guilin is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: =吳達善=吳達善，字雨民，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正紅旗人，陝西駐防。

translations.literal: Wu Dashan: Wu Dashan, courtesy name Yumin, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, garrisoned in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dashan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner garrisoned in Shaanxi; his courtesy name was Yumin.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He earned jinshi in the first year of Qianlong and was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 累擢至工部侍郎、鑲紅旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Board of Works and vice commander of the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to vice minister of the Board of Works and vice commander of the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was appointed governor of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, he was made governor of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 赴巴里坤督理軍需，以勞賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: He went to Barkol to supervise military supplies and, for his labor, was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Barkol to oversee military supplies, he was rewarded with a peacock feather for his exertions.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，疏言：「軍糧自肅州運哈密至軍，石需費十二、三兩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he memorialized, saying: "Military grain transported from Suzhou to Hami and then to the army costs twelve or thirteen taels per shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, he reported: "Moving army grain from Suzhou to Hami and on to the front costs twelve or thirteen taels per shi.

sentences.zh: 凱旋官兵糶口糧製衣履，請改二成本色，八成折價。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers returning in victory sell their ration grain to make clothes and shoes; I request changing this to twenty percent in kind and eighty percent at cash value.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious officers and soldiers were selling their rations to buy clothes and shoes; he asked that twenty percent be paid in kind and eighty percent in cash instead.

sentences.zh: 既得隨時支用，亦可稍省運費。」

translations.literal: They would thus be able to draw on it at any time, and transport costs could also be somewhat reduced."
translations.idiomatic: That would let them draw funds when needed and also save something on transport.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，代黃廷桂為陝甘總督，尋復以命楊應琚，改總督銜管巡撫事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he replaced Huang Tinggui as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu; soon the appointment was given instead to Yang Yingju, and he retained governor-general rank while managing provincial governor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he briefly replaced Huang Tinggui as governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu, but the post soon went to Yang Yingju; he kept governor-general rank while handling the governor's duties.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「寧夏橫城堡河漲城圮。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "At Hengcheng fort in Ningxia the river rose and the city wall collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "At Hengcheng fort in Ningxia, floodwaters breached the walls.

sentences.zh: 相度水勢，分別添築草壩，俾大溜北注，化險為平。」

translations.literal: Surveying the water's force, earthen dams were added in sections so that the main current would flow north, turning danger into safety."
translations.idiomatic: After gauging the current, he had earthen dams built in stages to turn the main flow northward and turn danger into safety.

sentences.zh: 旋以總督銜調河南巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to be governor of Henan with governor-general rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Henan, retaining governor-general rank.

sentences.zh: 奏改延津、封丘、胙城、滎澤、盧氏、靈寶諸縣營製，議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized changing the garrison organization of Yanjin, Fengqiu, Zuocheng, Xingze, Lushi, Lingbao, and other counties; the proposal was approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed reorganizing the garrisons in Yanjin, Fengqiu, Zuocheng, Xingze, Lushi, Lingbao, and other counties, and the plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，奏言：「雲南、貴州各鎮協營每兵千設藤牌兵百，少不適用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he memorialized, saying: "In each brigade and auxiliary garrison of Yunnan and Guizhou, a hundred rattan-shield soldiers were assigned per thousand troops—too few to be useful.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, he reported that in Yunnan and Guizhou each thousand-man garrison had only a hundred rattan-shield troops—too few to be effective.

sentences.zh: 請以七成改習鳥槍，三成改習弓箭。」

translations.literal: I request that seventy percent be changed to training in muskets and thirty percent to training in bow and arrow."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that seventy percent train with muskets and thirty percent with bow and arrow instead.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The change was approved.

sentences.zh: 尋兼署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also served concurrently as acting governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added acting governor of Yunnan to his duties.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，奏改都勻、銅仁二協營製。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he memorialized changing the organization of the two auxiliary garrisons at Duyun and Tongren.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, he reorganized the auxiliary garrisons at Duyun and Tongren.

sentences.zh: 調湖廣總督，兼署湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor-general of Huguang and also served concurrently as acting governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor-general of Huguang and also served as acting governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 巴陵民熊正朝偽稱縣人巡撫方顯子，居省城與紳士交結，乘間盜竊，捕得寘諸法。

translations.literal: Xiong Zhengchao, a commoner of Baling, falsely claimed to be the son of Governor Fang Xian, a native of the county; he lived in the provincial capital, associated with gentry, stole when opportunity arose, was captured, and punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Zhengchao, a commoner from Baling, passed himself off in the provincial capital as the son of Governor Fang Xian, mingled with local gentry, and stole whenever he saw a chance; once caught, he was punished by law.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，調陝甘總督，奏言：「木壘地廣土沃。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, he was transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu and memorialized, saying: "Mulei has broad territory and fertile soil.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu, he reported: "Mulei has wide lands and rich soil.

sentences.zh: 請將招集戶民編里分甲，裡選里長，百戶選渠長，鄉約保正。

translations.literal: I request that recruited settler households be organized into li and jia; within each li a li head should be chosen, among every hundred households a canal chief chosen, and village covenant wardens and baojia chiefs appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that recruited settlers be organized into li and jia, with li heads chosen within each li, canal chiefs among every hundred households, and local wardens and baojia chiefs appointed.

sentences.zh: 訟獄，守備審理；

translations.literal: For lawsuits, the garrison commandant should try them;
translations.idiomatic: Civil suits would be heard by the garrison commandant;

sentences.zh: 命盜案，守備驗訊。

translations.literal: for robbery and homicide cases, the garrison commandant should examine and interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: robbery and homicide cases would be investigated by the garrison commandant.

sentences.zh: 巴里坤同知審解。」

translations.literal: The subprefect of Barkol should review and remand."
translations.idiomatic: The Barkol subprefect would review and remand the cases.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，復調湖廣總督，兼署荊州將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, he was again transferred to governor-general of Huguang and also served concurrently as acting Jingzhou general.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year, he returned to governor-general of Huguang and also served as acting Jingzhou general.

sentences.zh: 命赴貴州，偕內閣學士富察善、侍郎錢維城按巡撫良卿、按察使高積營私骫法，論如律。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Guizhou and, together with Grand Secretariat Chancellor Fuca Shan and Vice Minister Qian Weicheng, investigate Governor Liang Qing and Provincial Judicial Commissioner Gao Ji for private gain and bending the law; they were sentenced according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Guizhou with Grand Secretariat Chancellor Fuca Shan and Vice Minister Qian Weicheng to investigate Governor Liang Qing and Provincial Judicial Commissioner Gao Ji for corruption and abuse of law; both were sentenced as the law required.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，兼署湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, he also served concurrently as acting governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, he also served as acting governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，復調陝甘總督，值土爾扈特部內附，上命分賚羊及皮衣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, he was again transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu; it happened that the Torghut tribe submitted to the dynasty, and the emperor ordered sheep and fur coats to be distributed in shares.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year, back as governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu, he took charge when the Torghuts submitted; the emperor ordered distribution of sheep and fur coats.

sentences.zh: 吳達善料理週妥，上嘉其能。

translations.literal: Wu Dashan handled the arrangements thoroughly and properly; the emperor praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dashan managed the distribution smoothly, and the emperor commended his competence.

sentences.zh: 以病乞解任。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested release from office.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to ask to be relieved of duty.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子太保，祀賢良祠，賜祭葬，諡勤毅。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined in the Temple of Worthies, granted funeral honors, posthumous title Qinyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, entered in the Temple of Worthies, granted state funeral honors, and given the posthumous name Qinyi, "Diligent and Resolute."

sentences.zh: =崔應階=崔應階，字吉升，湖北江夏人。

translations.literal: Cui Yingjie: Cui Yingjie, courtesy name Jisheng, a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yingjie, a native of Jiangxia in Hubei, bore the courtesy name Jisheng.

sentences.zh: 父相國，官浙江處州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: His father Xiangguo served as regional commander of Chuzhou garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiangguo was regional commander of the Chuzhou garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 應階，廕生。

translations.literal: Yingjie entered through yinsheng privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjie entered official life through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 初授順天府通判，遷西路同知。

translations.literal: He was first appointed assistant prefect of Shuntian prefecture and was transferred to be subprefect of the Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made assistant prefect of Shuntian and later transferred to subprefect of the Western Circuit.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，擢山西汾州知府。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period he was promoted to prefect of Fenzhou in Shanxi.
